issues.description: The assigned archive contains code, logs, the datasheet, and the appendix, but no raw XLSX/DTA source inputs. The datasheet specifies three raw files per experiment. The supplied Experiment 1 do-file directly imports/merges the main workbook, initial-survey file, and Prolific demographics file. The Experiment 2 do-file imports the adjusted main workbook and merges the initial-survey file; the separately listed payment-code/approval file is described as feeding the upstream manual ID correction and is not imported by the supplied Experiment 2 do-file. Complete input schemas and coverage remain unverified. The author-data routes are unverified; no explicit access barrier is evidenced.

The datasheet records a manual correction before the Experiment 2 Stata run, while the code consumes an adjusted workbook and does not include the crosswalk step. Clarify whether the supplied adjusted workbook already embodies that correction or provide the source/crosswalk and exact correction procedure. This is a preparation/contract gap, not evidence of a restricted license or access barrier.

The two Stata files refer to inputs under author-specific Windows directory roots. A portable working copy needs one coherent relative input root across each producer/consumer call; the directory components are omitted from quoted evidence.

evidence.description: Datasheet dates the initial and main surveys for both experiments.
evidence.quote:
We collected all experimental data via Qualtrics surveys. Experiment 1 used Prolific
   participants, recruited through the Prolific website. The initial survey was run on August 29,
   2024, while the main study was run on September 13, 2024. Experiment 2 used MTurk
   participants, recruited through the Amazon MTurk website. The initial survey was run on
   August 16, 2022, while the main study was run on August 29, 2022.

evidence.description: Datasheet states the initial and main sample counts, screening totals, follow-up timing, and Experiment 2 secondary-HIT inclusion.
evidence.quote:
All data was downloaded directly from Qualtrics on the aforementioned dates. As noted in
   Table 1 of the manuscript, 500 Prolific and 534 MTurk workers participated in the initial
   surveys for Experiment 1 and 2, respectively. We then analyzed those samples for bots and
   fraudulent submissions, flagging 22 observations from Prolific and 66 observations from
   MTurk for exclusion in our follow-up surveys. Two weeks after each initial survey, we
   collected observations from 250 Prolific and 251 MTurk workers for the main studies,
   recruited from each of the retained participant samples. As noted in the manuscript, we
   recruited 250 participants from our initial survey pools in each experiment. However, one
   MTurk participant in Experiment 2 completed the study on Qualtrics but timed out of the

   their payment and include them in the full sample for Experiment 2, resulting in 251

evidence.description: Datasheet specifies three raw files for each experiment and says the supplied Stata files convert and merge them.
evidence.quote:
Specifically, there were three raw files necessary for Experiment 1 (i.e., one for the initial
   survey, a second for the main study, and a third file provided directly by Prolific including
   participant demographic data), and three raw files for Experiment 2 (i.e., one for the initial
   survey, a second for the main study, and a third file provided directly by MTurk containing the
   payment codes and approvals for the main study). As discussed in Items #6 and #7 below, we
   provide the STATA Do Files and Logs for both Experiment 1 and Experiment 2 in the online
   material, which convert and merge these raw files into a single dataset for each experiment.

review_notes: The first populated checkpoint was saved after bounded environment metadata and named survey-platform catalog queries, then source review continued. This records the actual sequence and makes no claim of platform entitlement or input coverage.

Experiment 2's adjusted workbook and the raw-main-plus-payment-crosswalk reconstruction are alternative routes to the same corrected workbook input; do not make both routes mandatory when the adjusted workbook is supplied.
